subject: FinTechOps evals: recommended models & dataset/format next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fintechops.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@fintechops.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechOps evals: recommended models & dataset/format next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today

good call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the evals running on Redwood: 

Call recap (high level)
- You want a customer-specific eval to validate model fit on your customer support categorization + intent detection workload (sensitive PII redaction required).
- Success metric: combined intent accuracy + downstream routing F1; primary goal is to avoid regressions vs your current classifier.
- Scope: start with a 1k-sample gold set (we can do a 500-sample quick pass first).

Recommended Redwood models to evaluate (starter set)
- redwood-alpha-qa-1 (best latency/quality tradeoff for instruction-following tasks)
- rw-13b-quant (13B quantized variant

lower cost, good for throughput checks)
- open-llama-65b (reference large-model ceiling

if cost allows)

What we need from you
1) Sample dataset (CSV) with columns: prompt, reference, metadata (customer_id pseudonymized), label_intent. A 200-500 row sample is fine to start.
2) Scoring priorities: please confirm if intent accuracy is the only priority or if partial-match/slot extraction matters.
3) Any PII rules or redaction scripts we should apply before uploading.

Proposed Redwood setup & timeline
- We'll run a 500-sample quick-pass within a private eval workspace (VPC) using your sample data to check model fit and token costs.
- Deliverable: brief report + benchmark table + example failure cases and prompt set recommendations. Target: 3 business days after receiving sample.

Attachments I'm including: fintechops_sample_dataset_v1.csv (schema example), redwood_model_benchmarks_q3_2027.pdf (benchmarks/latency docs), eval_sow_v0.3.docx (SOW draft).

Next steps
- Can you share the sample CSV and confirm whether we should run the quick-pass in Private (VPC) or if a dedicated-hosted eval is acceptable?
- I'll loop in Dev (infra) and Dylan (SE) once we have the sample to schedule the run.

Thanks


Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fintechops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@fintechops.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechOps evals: recommended models & dataset/format next steps

Marissa

thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications below and we'll share a sample by EOD today.

- PII: We cannot share raw customer emails or any direct identifiers. We'll pseudonymize customer_id and run a redaction pass to remove email addresses and SSNs. We'll also add a metadata flag for "contains_sensitive" where applicable.
- Scoring: Primary metric is intent accuracy (micro-avg). Secondary: slot extraction F1 for the top 5 intents. If redwood has an embedding-similarity fallback metric for partial matches, that would be useful.
- Environment: We prefer Private (VPC) for the quick-pass because the data will still contain sensitive fields even after redaction. Can you confirm you can spin a private eval workspace?

Also

are there any constraints on input length/tokenization we should be aware of for the sample? Our longest examples are ~1.5k tokens after concatenation.

Subject: Fwd: FinTechOps evals: recommended models & dataset/format next steps

Hi Dev / Dylan

-forwarding Sanjay's confirmation. They will provide a pseudonymized CSV sample today and prefer a Private (VPC) eval workspace. Please see details below and let me know feasibility and ETA for provisioning.

Key asks for the infra/SE run:
- Provision a Private eval workspace in us-west-2 with access for FinTechOps test users (SAML invite will follow).
- Install the eval harness with the following dataset format expectations: CSV with columns: prompt (string), reference (string), label_intent (string), customer_id (pseudonymized), contains_sensitive (boolean), notes (optional). UTF-8, comma separated.
- Scoring criteria (to implement):
  * Intent accuracy (primary)

  micro-averaged accuracy across intents
  * Slot extraction

  token-level F1 for defined slots (top 5 intents)
  * Partial-match metric: embedding-similarity

  cosine threshold 0.82 to mark near-matches
  * Regression check: compare against baseline classifier results supplied by FinTechOps (they'll attach baseline results JSON)
- Models to run: redwood-alpha-qa-1, rw-13b-quant, open-llama-65b (if capacity/approval). Please run with default decoding (top-p=0.95, temp=0.2) and a deterministic seed for reproducibility.
- Resource controls: enable prefix/KV caching off for the first pass to capture cold-start behavior; capture token counts per request for cost estimation.
- Deliverables: results table (per-model accuracy/F1), failure-case examples (10 per model), cost estimate (tokenized cost) and a short recommendations doc.

Timeline: once sample is uploaded we should be able to run a 500-sample quick-pass within 48-72 hours. If any of the model runs exceed expected GPU time/cost, flag before proceeding.

Attachments: sample schema attached (fintechops_sample_dataset_v1.csv).

Thanks


Best,
Marissa

Thanks

- quick update from the SE side.

I'll provision the private eval workspace in us-west-2 today and set up the eval harness. Plan:
- Run a 500-sample quick-pass using redwood-alpha-qa-1 and rw-13b-quant (open-llama-65b will be a follow-up if requested).
- Scoring implementation: intent accuracy + token-level slot F1 + embedding-sim partial-match (cosine >= 0.82). I'll wire up a regression comparator to their baseline.
- I'll disable prefix/KV caching for the initial run and capture token counts + latency metrics.
- Expected ETA: first pass results & concise report by Mon, 20 Sep 2027 COB. If we hit any dataset or privacy blockers I'll pause and flag.

On the sample length: 1.5k tokens max is fine - I'll cap generation context to 2048 tokens for the initial runs. If we need >2048 we can discuss segmenting examples or using a longer-context variant.

Attaching the run checklist to the workspace and I'll share the notebook link once deployed: https://drive.redwood.ai/fintechops/eval-notebook
